nonblocking_findings.title: Execution prerequisites and outcomes remain unproved
nonblocking_findings.details: The actual supplied artifacts are source, historical R2 admission/launch records and prior source audits. nonblocking_findings.title: Finite fixture scope cannot establish learned-C performance
nonblocking_findings.details: The prospective test is one fixed Train sequence, seed2027, two 256-frame continuing histories on one visible GPU, plus one local constant0 step at each actual original-qualified write. It is neither 256 frames of an always-reject policy nor a learned-C evaluation. At 50-frame cadence, possible test events are frames50/100/150/200/250; success requires at least one actual qualified write and every such write is checked. track_calls=512+writes counts tracker.step invocations only, conditionally 513..517 for a successful run. Native/CLIP initialization forwards and the frozen reference projection are additional work; track_calls must not be mislabeled as the number of all neural submodule forwards. Exact equality in this window would establish local native-path consistency only. It would not validate learned C initialization/training, negative/zero/unknown-label handling on actual teacher samples, development32 own-history behavior, the fixed-teacher causal-label coverage on changed histories, full recursive development, Full152 final training or official nine metrics. Prior v3 scope limits remain unchanged.
nonblocking_findings.required_action: Label any later successful result as one-sequence constant-action consistency only; separately complete and audit C training, own-history development and final metrics.

The supplied training_spec records the actual Train root, 2576 paired frames, valid first box [269,248,33,32] and GT SHA. context binds the spec to the historical trained result, final checkpoint, human-confirmed bank/labels and native/CLIP weights. image reads RGB/depth files; frames 1..256 are exactly the first 256 noninitialization frames (image files 2..257). There is one initialization per history, no reset after frame0, no load_truth/loadtxt call on this entry path and no GT-based frame/event selection. The imported pilot module defines GT-reading helpers, but only context is called here; its collection/replay/main bodies are not executed on import. C inputs remain current and previous selected features, the fixed first-frame reference, predicted quality/confidence and predicted motion. No current/future GT, future image or teacher utility is used by either constant fixture. The physical dataset files were not opened by this reviewer.

It tests exact torch.equal, numpy.array_equal and record equality with an explicitly identified control. It never divides a metric by prediction statistics. Constant1 accepts every original-qualified write, constant0 rejects it under the existing future >0 rule; neither changes the selected current box, query, feature or score. technical_source_checks.title: Independent continuing histories
technical_source_checks.details: actor and other, and their native tracker objects, are different objects. Each native initialize replaces its state list, template list/patch, query=None and frame0. FullDenseTracker.initialize rebuilds its initial dictionary and feature tensors from that independent initialization; observe produces new converted features, masks and origins. The source explicitly checks state/list/patch/initial-dictionary identity separation, cross-history template data_ptr separation and equal initial tensor values. Model, decoder, preprocessing constants and immutable word/reference data may be shared. The initial reference is read-only; there is no initial-evidence mutation in the called decoder/reference path. This is a source ownership assessment, not a runtime pointer witness. Historical bound native initializer SHA agrees with the R2 gate.

technical_source_checks.title: Original outputs and mutable state cloned before wrapped forward
technical_source_checks.details: All original_out tensors are detached/cloned on their current device at133. copy_tracker_state at134 owns the bbox list, native object, template tensor storage (preserving the initial-slot alias), patch array, recurrent query tensors and selected feature. saved_history at135 independently clones the query and feature to CPU. Only then does wrapped.step run at138. Equality compares the wrapped state to that immutable post-step snapshot; line144 also compares the live original actor to its snapshot, so a wrapped call that mutates the original mutable history cannot silently make both sides equal. Initial evidence/model state are shared read-only within snapshot copies; the existing helper states this explicitly.

technical_source_checks.title: Full RNG tuple checks and sequential restore
technical_source_checks.details: capture_rng/restore_rng cover Python random, the full NumPy get_state tuple, Torch CPU and the current visible CUDA device byte state. assert_same_rng checks the NumPy algorithm, full key array, position, Gaussian flag and cached Gaussian, plus complete CPU/CUDA state tensors. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES must equal the one selected physical GPU string, so the current-device state is the single visible device used here; this is not an all-GPU experiment. RNG is restored before each independent initialization/step and each reject probe, compared after those calls, and restored to the original trajectory state before advancing. Nine isolated stdlib Boolean-oracle cases (identical plus eight perturbed fields) confirm field-check coverage only; no native RNG or tensor comparison was executed.

technical_source_checks.title: Actual qualification and pre-step reject copy
technical_source_checks.details: A separate mutable copy of other is made before either step at each possible 50-frame write boundary. It is used only if the independently executed original record actually says template_write=True. It therefore includes the pre-event query, previous selected feature, prior bbox and both prior templates. The reject branch starts with the same pre-step RNG and frozen first-frame reference, reruns the same frame once, and checks qualification and fixture0 explicitly. Current output/record, bbox/frame, query, feature and C input agree with constant1; saved prior templates and patch remain exactly equal after rejection. The reject branch does not replace either continuing history.

technical_source_checks.title: C gates only the qualified template crop/write
technical_source_checks.details: The v3 tracker source is unchanged and preserves the FullDenseTracker selection, pixel geometry, candidate-field checks, query and score path. It computes the original qualification from frame interval and selected-position native confidence, computes C inputs/prediction/accepts_write only for qualified frames, then enters the template crop/preprocess/append/pop block only when accepted. Constant0 uses the future arm and 0>0 is false. The current output/query has already been assigned before that decision. There is no score rescaling or alternate candidate selection. Constant1 uses the same crop/write path as the original.

technical_source_checks.title: Frozen shared state and auditable raw artifacts
technical_source_checks.details: context puts decoder/native/CLIP into eval and disables their gradients. main is no_grad, fixtures have no parameters, and the wrapper requires nontraining frozen writer/model state. Before/after native+CLIP state_dict digests and decoder digests must match after the full run. Raw histories persist all256 original and constant1 records, exact CPU-cloned recurrent queries and selected features; qualified rejection entries persist their record/query/feature, C input, retained templates and patch. records.jsonl additionally holds both main records per frame. The receipt binds raw PT/JSONL, inputs, teacher/audit and preflight/tracker/feature source SHAs. It does not persist every decoder output tensor or full per-frame template history; full output equality is asserted in-run, and no stronger raw-artifact claim is made.

original_finding.title: Development comparison drops the audited teacher/native-prefix provenance chain
original_finding.details: Training binds its aggregate and replay-shard results to the terminal audit and records both teacher_result_sha256 and teacher_audit_sha256. The analyzer instead accepts a teacher root by completion status, exit code, spec and shared model-input metadata. It merely computes the current native_prefix.jsonl hash, without comparing it to an audited expected hash. It also never reads the fit results' teacher_result_sha256 or teacher_audit_sha256. Matching input/model metadata and comparing the two arms' common_dataset_sha256 do not establish that the native comparison trajectories came from the same audited teacher that produced the fit data. This is a concrete missing provenance join at the metric consumer; it is not an allegation that the unexecuted results are already corrupted.
original_finding.necessary_fix: Change only the new R3 analyzer: require the actual terminal R2 audit; require completed/zero-blocker/terminal-raw-audit flags; compare the aggregate SHA to audited_teacher_result_sha256; compare each native-prefix SHA to that same audit's per-shard native-prefix hashes; and require each fit result's teacher_result_sha256 and teacher_audit_sha256 to equal those exact inputs. The future terminal audit must emit the per-shard expected prefix hashes. Do not modify or restart the currently running R2 sources. Preserve this v2 report and source snapshots, then audit the revised R3 input version.
